facts.statement: Bavaricarbo is a new genus whose type species is B. brevirostris.
facts.quote: The type species is B. brevirostris.

facts.statement: It belongs to the stem group of the cormorant family Phalacrocoracidae.
facts.quote: A member of the stem group of Phalacrocoracidae.

facts.statement: Bavaricarbo is an extinct cormorant from the Miocene.
facts.quote: Bavaricarbo is an extinct genus of cormorant (family Phalacrocoracidae) from the Miocene

facts.statement: Its fossils come from the Hammerschmiede clay pit in Germany.
It was named in 2026 by Mayr, Lechner and Böhme in the Swiss Journal of Palaeontology.
facts.quote:
Journal: Swiss Journal of Palaeontology
Year: 2026
Authors: Gerald Mayr, Thomas Lechner, Madelaine Böhme

facts.statement: The naming study describes it as a cormorant with a short beak.
facts.quote: A new short-beaked stem group cormorant (Phalacrocoracidae)

facts.statement: The same study reports a new hawk, a small swift and other birds from the Hammerschmiede site, which also yields hominid fossils, dating to the early Late Miocene.
facts.quote: an unusual new hawk (Accipitridae), a small swift (Apodidae), and other avian remains from the early Late Miocene hominid Fossil-Lagerstätte Hammerschmiede

sentences.text: Bavaricarbo was a cormorant with a short beak that lived during the Miocene.
Its remains were found in the Hammerschmiede clay pit in Germany.
Mayr, Lechner and Böhme named it in 2026 in the Swiss Journal of Palaeontology.
It sits in the stem group of the cormorant family Phalacrocoracidae, that is, outside the group formed by living cormorants.
Its only species is Bavaricarbo brevirostris.
The same site, which has also yielded fossils of ancient hominids, preserves a new hawk, a small swift and other birds from the early Late Miocene.
Bavaricarbo fue un cormorán de pico corto que vivió durante el Mioceno.
Sus restos se hallaron en la cantera de arcilla de Hammerschmiede, en Alemania.
Mayr, Lechner y Böhme le dieron nombre en 2026 en la revista Swiss Journal of Palaeontology.
Se sitúa en el grupo troncal de la familia de los cormoranes, Phalacrocoracidae, es decir, fuera del grupo que forman los cormoranes actuales.
Su única especie es Bavaricarbo brevirostris.
El mismo yacimiento, que también ha proporcionado fósiles de homínidos antiguos, conserva una nueva ave rapaz, un vencejo pequeño y otras aves de comienzos del Mioceno Superior.
